A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QVF research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and some figure-label errors in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulator experiments on image and 3D shape representation, architecture ablations, circuit noise, finite-shot measurement, and completion tasks.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: The energy-based amplitude encoding, real-valued quantum circuit, local measurements, training objective, and latent-code inference remain unchanged. Although Section 4.1 now describes only the ReLU encoder, the sine-based configurations remain in the experiments; this omission does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR-10 images, the astronomical image examples, ShapeNet geometries, and the same representation, interpolation, inpainting, completion, and noise scenarios. Removing the explicit four-image astronomical experiment sentence does not remove its retained visual results.

E2.justification: QIREN remains the comparator in Table 2, and ReLU/DeepSDF and sine-based classical models remain in Table 3. The handcrafted encoding comparison also remains in Section 5.2. Changing table labels from Siren to Sin does not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: The 50-image evaluations, three shapes with 100,000 samples each, circuit configuration, 5,000 training epochs, optimizer schedule, metrics, and masking/noise settings are retained. Defaults removed from the main text remain in Appendix B.2. Naming the simulator backend adds documentation rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The gradient comparison, circuit-depth/qubit/width ablations, finite-shot and noisy-gate tests, inpainting, noisy-depth completion, and geometric-error visualizations are retained. Their relocation and expanded interpretation do not add or remove an experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report metrics averaged over three repetitions and retain the same plus/minus reporting and uncertainty bands. V2 introduces no new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their numerical entries, and the corresponding plots and reconstructions retain their outcomes. For example, Table 2 still reports PSNR 32.67±0.3 for identity-initialized QVF with sine activation and 31.03±0.2 for QIREN. Figure redesigns do not change these results.

T1.justification: Section 5 generalizes the simulator complexity statement from O(2^(3n)J) to O(2^(cn)J), with c depending on the simulation method. Appendix D explicitly adds the inverse-shot-count variance relation. The Fourier review and expressiveness lemma already existed in v1's appendices and are moved into the main text.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claim from outperforming classical foundational baselines to competing with them, while retaining superiority over the quantum comparator. The conclusion removes the claim of training faster than all compared methods. The principal architectural contributions and supported applications remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies robust scaling as applying to the evaluated scenario and expands the explanation of finite-shot noise. Appendix G newly attributes geometric improvements to spectral connections, while omitting v1 Appendix I's explicit discussion of balancing classical-network capacity and quantum resources.

D1.justification: V2 names the PennyLane default.qubit.torch backend and changes the implementation statement from a future release to reported availability on the project page. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit Gaussian latent-code initialization and the A100's 40 GB memory specification. These are documentation changes, not demonstrated experimental changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds Meli et al.'s quantum-enhanced computer vision survey, replaces the COIN discussion with a fuller NeRF description, and removes the extended appendix discussion of sandwich architectures and several supporting references. The central positioning against QIREN and 3D-QAE remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and numerous technical passages are rewritten. The Fourier review replaces the main-text quantum-computing primer, the expressiveness lemma moves into Section 4.1, the appendices are substantially reorganized, and an author-contributions paragraph is added. This materially changes the narrative organization despite stable methodology and experiments.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to a single-column layout with extensively resized and wrapped figures and tables. Figure 6 gains axis and panel labels, and Figure 1's panels are relabeled. V2 also introduces duplicate appendix Figure 12/13 numbers and leaves stale references to Figure 1's interpolation panel.

improvement.justification: V2 improves claim calibration, brings existing theoretical material into the main narrative, and reports implementation availability. However, it removes explicit initialization details and introduces duplicate figure numbers and stale panel references, weakening reproducibility and navigation. With the method and empirical evidence retained, these competing reporting benefits and regressions do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
